summary: Authentication that handles itself — every auth method as typed data, OAuth flows that run end-to-end, tokens that refresh automatically, credentials stored securely.
the_vision: Authentication in data applications is plumbing that everyone rebuilds. OAuth flows, token refresh, credential storage, multi-tenant token isolation — the same patterns, reimplemented for every integration. mountainash-auth-client makes authentication declarative: pick an auth type as typed data, and the library handles the flow, the lifecycle, and the storage.

what_it_makes_possible.capability: Every auth method as typed data
what_it_makes_possible.essence: OAuth2 with PKCE, OAuth1, IAM, Azure AD, Kerberos, certificates, service accounts, passwords, tokens, JWT, and 'none' — each is a Pydantic model with validated fields and SecretStr-protected credentials. Pick the right one for your backend. The discriminated union ensures type safety across the entire ecosystem.

OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE runs end-to-end: open the browser, capture the callback, exchange the code, store the tokens. OAuth 1.0a handles the three-legged flow for legacy APIs. Browser-based and manual redirect modes. The flow runs once, then tokens refresh automatically.

Connection mixins handle the full token lifecycle — load from storage, check expiry, refresh if possible, re-authorize if needed. File-locked concurrent refresh prevents race conditions in multi-process pipelines. Token migration from inline config to secure storage happens transparently.

Secure filesystem storage with restricted permissions, symlink rejection, atomic writes, and fcntl locking. Domain-namespaced paths isolate tokens per provider and user. The SecretStore protocol accepts custom backends for organisations that need Vault or KMS.

Building an integration with an OAuth2 or OAuth1 provider? The connection mixins give you connect/disconnect lifecycle management, automatic token refresh, and secure storage — out of the box. Define the provider's metadata (URLs, scopes, flags) and the mixin handles the rest.

use_cases.title: The multi-provider data pipeline
use_cases.story: A pipeline ingests from Garmin (OAuth1), Google Health (OAuth2 with PKCE), and Strava (OAuth2). Each provider has different auth requirements. One auth library handles all three — flows, token refresh, secure storage. The pipeline code deals with data, not authentication plumbing.

use_cases.title: Multi-tenant credential isolation
use_cases.story: A SaaS platform manages data connections for multiple users, each with their own OAuth tokens for different providers. Domain-namespaced storage isolates credentials per user per provider. Token refresh happens per-user with file locking to prevent concurrent refresh races.

use_cases.title: The migration from inline credentials
use_cases.story: Legacy config files have OAuth tokens inline. mountainash-auth-client detects inline tokens, migrates them to the secure store, and replaces them with store references — transparently, on first connection. No manual migration step.
